school: 二十世纪苏联理论物理的立法者兼最高考官：1908 年生于巴库一个石油工程师家庭，14 岁入巴库大学，19 岁转列宁格勒大学，1927 年毕业，1929-1931 年持洛克菲勒奖学金游学欧洲——在哥廷根、莱比锡（海森堡门下）、苏黎世（泡利门下）、哥本哈根（玻尔门下）受训，自称一生'唯一的女弟子'是玻尔；1932 年任哈尔科夫乌克兰物理技术研究所理论部负责人，创立研讨班与理论最低标准考试；1937 年应卡皮察之邀迁莫斯科物理问题研究所，任理论部负责人；1938 年因反斯大林传单被捕入狱一年，卡皮察以生命担保营救出狱；1937-1941 年间完成三件改写物理的事：以序参量自由能展开建立二级相变的唯象理论（1937），以二流体模型解释液氦超流并预言第二声（1941，获诺贝尔奖的核心工作），与栗弗席兹合写《理论物理学教程》第一卷；1950 年与金兹堡提出超导的金兹堡-朗道方程；1962 年 1 月车祸重伤，此后六年不能执笔，靠口述与弟子合作继续产出——同年获诺贝尔物理学奖（超流理论），因伤不能赴斯德哥尔摩，由瑞典大使在莫斯科授奖；其'理论最低标准'考试一生只放行约四十人，1950 年代起以一张分级表给物理学家定级（牛顿 0 级、爱因斯坦 1 级、玻尔等 2 级、自评 2.5 级后升至 2 级）；1968 年 4 月 1 日病逝莫斯科，身后朗道十诫、朗道能级、朗道阻尼、朗道-金兹堡理论、朗道符号（大 O 记号的现代用法）皆以其命名——他证明：一个学派最深的财富不是成果而是标准
historical_significance: 朗道（Lev Davidovich Landau，1908-1968），1908 年 1 月 22 日生于巴库，父亲是里海石油公司的工程师；天资早慧，13 岁读完中学课程，14 岁入巴库大学，1924 年转列宁格勒大学物理系，1927 年 19 岁毕业并进列宁格勒物理技术研究所；1929 年获洛克菲勒奖学金游学欧洲一年半——哥廷根、莱比锡（海森堡）、苏黎世（泡利，泡利说他'给这个爱嘲弄的苏联人一点点物理学，他回报以加倍的嘲弄'）、剑桥（卢瑟福实验室，经卡皮察引见）、哥本哈根（玻尔研究所，1930 与 1933 两度长驻）——玻尔对他影响最深，他终生自称'玻尔的学生'；1931 年回国，1932 年任哈尔科夫乌克兰物理技术研究所理论部负责人，年方二十四：他首创理论物理的考试纪律——'理论最低标准'（теорминимум）七门笔试加口试，通过者才配做他的研究生，一生通过者约四十人；同时建立每周一次的'朗道研讨班'，规矩是任何人念论文不得跳行，朗道以摧毁式提问当场处决含糊之处——'不必体面，要正确'；1937 年应卡皮察之邀任莫斯科苏联科学院物理问题研究所理论部负责人；1938 年 4 月因参与起草反斯大林传单被捕，卡皮察上书贝利亚与莫洛托夫以自身担保，1939 年 5 月出狱——此后他再不过问政治，只做物理；其科学产出横跨理论物理全部领域（他晚年宣称'已经不做物理了，因为剩下的都是肮脏的部分'的说法反证其全面）：1937 年二级相变的序参量展开理论——把对称破缺写成一条自由能多项式，预言临界指数，成为此后一切相变理论（含重整化群）的出发点；1941 年液氦超流的二流体模型——把超流写成一种无熵的量子流体与正常流体的混合，预言第二声并在同年被实验证实，此文是他 1962 年诺贝尔奖的核心；1946 年等离子体振荡的朗道阻尼——无碰撞阻尼的预言被其后实验确证；1950 年与金兹堡提出超导的金兹堡-朗道方程——日后阿布里科索夫由它推出第二类超导体的磁通格子；1948-1953 年（应苏联氢弹工程之需）参与计算，贡献保密；与栗弗席兹合著的《理论物理学教程》十卷（1940 年起，1976 年前出齐）以'物理学家只该读这一套'的野心统一了全球理论物理的教学语言，被译成二十余种文字；1950 年代起他持一张分级表给物理学家定级：牛顿独占 0 级，爱因斯坦 1 级，玻尔、薛定谔、海森堡、狄拉克等 2 级，自评 2.5 级（后升 2 级）——此表流传至今，成为科学史上最著名的傲慢与自省混合物；1962 年 1 月 7 日车祸重伤，六次临床死亡被救回，此后终身不能执笔——他靠口述让弟子代笔继续产出论文；同年 11 月因超流理论获诺贝尔物理学奖，不能赴斯德哥尔摩，颁奖礼移至莫斯科瑞典使馆举行；1968 年 4 月 1 日病逝莫斯科；身后以他命名者有朗道能级、朗道阻尼、朗道-金兹堡理论、朗道-栗弗席兹方程、费米液体中的朗道参数、朗道符号（大 O 记号）；其学派（栗弗席兹、哈利特尼科夫、阿布里科索夫、戈尔科夫、米格达尔、克利什等）垄断苏联理论物理数十年——他证明：成果会过时，标准不会
historical_significance_en: Lev Davidovich Landau (1908-1968) was born in Baku on 22 January 1908, his father an engineer with the Caspian oil company; precocious to the point of legend, he finished secondary school at thirteen, entered Baku University at fourteen, moved to Leningrad University's physics department in 1924, and graduated at nineteen in 1927, joining the Leningrad Physicotechnical Institute. In 1929 a Rockefeller fellowship took him on an eighteen-month tour of Europe — Göttingen, Leipzig (Heisenberg), Zurich (Pauli, who said he gave 'the mocking Russian a little physics and received in return a double dose of mockery'), Cambridge (through Kapitsa's introduction to Rutherford's laboratory) and twice to Copenhagen (Bohr's institute, 1930 and 1933) — Bohr influenced him most, and Landau called himself Bohr's pupil all his life. Home in 1931, in 1932, aged twenty-four, he became head of the theory division at the Ukrainian Physicotechnical Institute in Kharkov: there he invented the examination discipline of theoretical physics — a 'theoretical minimum' of written and oral tests that a student had to pass to become his pupil; about forty people passed in his lifetime. He also founded the weekly Landau seminar, whose rule was that no reader of a paper might skip a line while Landau executed vagueness with destructive questions — 'one need not be polite; one must be correct'. In 1937 Kapitsa brought him to Moscow as head of the theory division of the Institute for Physical Problems; in April 1938 he was arrested for taking part in drafting an anti-Stalin leaflet, and Kapitsa staked his own life in letters to Beria and Molotov to free him in May 1939 — Landau never touched politics again. His output covered every province of theoretical physics: in 1937 the theory of second-order phase transitions as an expansion of free energy in an order parameter, which fixed the critical exponents and became the starting point of all later transition theory including the renormalization group; in 1941 the two-fluid model of superfluidity in liquid helium — a superfluid written as an entropy-free quantum liquid mixed with a normal fluid, predicting second sound, confirmed the same year, and the core of his 1962 Nobel Prize; in 1946 Landau damping of plasma oscillations, a prediction without collisions later confirmed by experiment; in 1950 the Ginzburg-Landau equations of superconductivity with Ginzburg, from which Abrikosov later derived the flux lattice of type-II superconductors; classified work on the Soviet hydrogen-bomb program in 1948-53. With Lifshitz he wrote the ten-volume Course of Theoretical Physics (from 1940), written with the ambition that 'a physicist need read nothing else', translated into two dozen languages, which unified the teaching language of theoretical physics worldwide. From the 1950s he graded physicists on a scale: Newton alone at 0, Einstein at 1, Bohr, Schrödinger, Heisenberg and Dirac at 2, himself at 2.5 (later raised to 2) — the most famous mixture of arrogance and self-audit in the history of science. On 7 January 1962 a car crash nearly killed him — he was clinically dead six times and revived — and he could never write again; he dictated to pupils, who drafted the papers. In November 1962 the Nobel Prize for superfluidity was awarded, and as he could not travel, the ceremony was held in the Swedish embassy in Moscow. He died in Moscow on 1 April 1968. Landau levels, Landau damping, Ginzburg-Landau theory, the Landau-Lifshitz equation, Landau parameters of Fermi liquids and the Landau notation (big-O) all bear his name; his school — Lifshitz, Khalatnikov, Abrikosov, Gorkov, Migdal and others — dominated Soviet theoretical physics for decades. He proved that results age, but standards do not.
unique_thinking: 朗道的独特处在于三重'标准的立法'：第一，入口立法——他不设计多么精妙的培养方案，只设一道门：理论最低标准考试，九门课，十分钟口试，'不懂就是不懂'，一生只放行约四十人——他证明学派的质量等于入口的质量，而入口的质量等于考官敢刷掉多少人；第二，现场立法——朗道研讨班不许念稿跳行、不许用'显然'蒙混，含糊当场被处决，他自己也接受同样火力——他证明批评的纪律必须是双向的，否则就只是权术；第三，谱系立法——0 到 5 的分级表表面是傲慢，内里是一份精确的自我定位文件：他把牛顿放 0、爱因斯坦放 1、自己放 2.5，等于公开宣称'我的尺度能容纳比我高一截半的人'——他证明给整个领域定坐标系的人，坐标系最终也定义他自己；此外他是'纸上理论家'的原型：理论物理用铅笔和纸就够，仪器只是理论的下游
unique_thinking_en: Landau's singularity is a triple legislation of standards. First, legislating the entrance: he devised no elaborate pedagogy but a single gate — the theoretical minimum, nine subjects, ten-minute orals, 'what you do not know, you do not know' — and in his lifetime passed only about forty people: a school's quality equals the quality of its entrance, and the entrance's quality equals the number the examiner dares fail. Second, legislating the live moment: at the Landau seminar no reader might skip a line and no one might hide behind 'obviously'; vagueness was executed on the spot, and he took the same fire himself — the discipline of criticism must run both ways or it is only politics. Third, legislating the genealogy: the 0-to-5 scale looks like arrogance but is in fact a precise document of self-location — Newton at 0, Einstein at 1, himself at 2.5 is a public declaration that his scale has room for people half a class above him; he who fixes the coordinates of a whole field is finally defined by his own coordinates. He was also the prototype of the paper-only theorist: theoretical physics needs pencil and paper, and instruments are downstream of theory.
civilization_zh: 二十世纪三十至六十年代的莫斯科——一个自称'最后一位全能理论物理学家'的人在苏联建立起历史上最严格的理论物理学派：他以十分钟口试的'理论最低标准'筛选门徒，以一张 0 到 5 的分级表给全世界的物理学家定级，以十卷《理论物理学教程》铸成整个学科的通用语言——他就是证明'理论的纪律可以像公理一样传承'的人
civilization_en: Moscow from the 1930s to the 1960s — a man who called himself the last universal theorist built the strictest school of theoretical physics in the Soviet Union: he filtered disciples through a ten-minute oral exam called the 'theoretical minimum', graded the world's physicists on a scale from 0 to 5, and cast the common language of an entire discipline in his ten-volume Course of Theoretical Physics — proof that the discipline of theory can be handed down like an axiom

cross_references.description_zh: 朗道与爱因斯坦同走'纸上演绎'的路：两人都相信理论物理的最高工序是铅笔与纸，仪器与实验只是下游；爱因斯坦把直觉变成原理，朗道把原理变成标准与考试——两人都留下了一套后人绕不开的体系（相对论 / 理论物理学教程与最低标准）——平行命题：理论家有两种遗产，一种是以问题替世界立法，一种是以标准替学科立法。
cross_references.description_en: Landau and Einstein walked the same road of deduction on paper: both held that the highest operation of theoretical physics is pencil and paper, with instruments and experiment downstream; Einstein turned intuition into principles, Landau turned principles into standards and examinations — and both left behind systems later comers could not bypass (relativity; the Course of Theoretical Physics and the theoretical minimum) — the parallel thesis: a theorist leaves two kinds of legacy, laws for the world posed as problems, or laws for a discipline posed as standards.

cross_references.description_zh: 朗道与高斯代表了数学科学家的两种沉默：高斯把最深的工作藏进抽屉，等死后发表——沉默是为了体系的完美；朗道把最严的火力开在公开研讨班上，当场处决含糊——发声是为了现场的正确；高斯的朋友圈越窄产出越纯，朗道的门徒越严学派越大——对照命题：立法者可以选择藏与考，但标准必须先于成果存在——高斯的标准写在他未发表的稿子里，朗道的标准写在他放行的四十个人的名单里。
cross_references.description_en: Landau and Gauss stand for two silences of the mathematical scientist: Gauss hid his deepest work in a drawer and published it after death — silence in service of the system's perfection; Landau opened his fiercest fire in a public seminar and executed vagueness on the spot — speech in service of correctness in the moment; the narrower Gauss's circle, the purer his output; the stricter Landau's pupils, the larger his school — the contrast thesis: a legislator may choose to hide or to examine, but standards must precede results — Gauss's standards live in his unpublished manuscripts, Landau's in the list of the forty he passed.

cross_references.description_zh: 朗道与牛顿都以一人之力为一门学科铸成通用语言：牛顿的《原理》为力学立法，朗道的十卷《教程》为理论物理立法；两人都是分级表上的极端（朗道把牛顿独放 0 级），都相信学科的统一来自一套可传授的公理与格式；差异在于牛顿独断独行、晚年以权术护标准，朗道以考试与研讨班把标准变成可以复制的制度——平行命题：一门成熟学科的标志，是它的新人从同一套书、同一张清单、同一种严苛里走出来。
cross_references.description_en: Landau and Newton each forged the common language of a discipline single-handed: Newton's Principia legislated mechanics, Landau's ten-volume Course legislated theoretical physics; both occupy the extremes of a grading scale (Landau left Newton alone at 0), and both believed a science's unity comes from one teachable set of axioms and formats; the difference is that Newton ruled alone and guarded standards with power in old age, while Landau turned standards into a replicable institution through examinations and seminars — the parallel thesis: a mature science is one whose newcomers all walk out of the same books, the same checklist, the same severity.
